title: Set up dimensionless grid
action: Set the speed parameter q = 0.04 directly. Define a polar grid for integration: radial coordinate ρ from 0.1 to 10 (use, for example, 50 logarithmically spaced points to capture the peak of the integrand). Angular coordinate θ from 0 to 2π (e.g., 24 points at 15° increments, mirroring the paper's evaluation increments). Store the grid arrays for later use.
description: Dimensionless grid setup for numerical integration.

title: Compute Mathieu functions
action: Evaluate the angular Mathieu functions for the first mode using scipy.special. For each grid point (ρ,θ), compute ω = θ - π/4. ce₁(ω) = scipy.special.mathieu_cem(1, q, ω)[0]. se₁(ω) = scipy.special.mathieu_sem(1, q, ω)[0]. For radial hyperbolic Mathieu functions of the second kind that vanish at infinity, use scipy.special.mathieu_modcem2 and mathieu_modsem2 with argument z = ln(ρ) for ρ ≥ 1. Determine the scaling factor C by evaluating the raw even function and the Bessel function I₁ at a small reference ρ (e.g., ρ=0.1): C = 2 * scipy.special.iv(1, √q / ρ_ref) / raw_even(ρ_ref). Then set Fek₁*(ρ) = C * scipy.special.mathieu_modcem2(1, q, ln ρ)[0] and Gek₁*(ρ) = C * scipy.special.mathieu_modsem2(1, q, ln ρ)[0]. For ρ < 1 use the symmetry Fek₁*(ρ) = Gek₁*(1/ρ).
description: Numerical evaluation of the special functions needed for ψ.

title: Compute concentration field
action: For each grid point (ρ,θ) evaluate E = exp( (√q / ρ) sinθ + √q ρ cosθ ). ψ = E - √2 * ce₁(ω) * Fek₁*(ρ) - √2 * se₁(ω) * Gek₁*(ρ). Compute c/c₀ = ψ * exp( -(√q / ρ) sinθ - √q ρ cosθ ). Compute perturbation Q = (c/c₀) * exp( (2√q / ρ) sinθ ) - 1.
description: Construction of the concentration perturbation field.

title: Integration of perturbation force
action: Numerically integrate the perturbation force integral over ρ and θ to obtain the dimensionless force factor F/(A μ c₀). The integrand is: - exp(-V/kT) * Q * (sin 2θ / ρ), with V/kT = (2√q / ρ) sinθ. Integrate over ρ from 0.1 to 10 and θ from 0 to 2π using 2D numerical integration (e.g., Simpson's rule or scipy.integrate.simps). Save the result in force_factor.json.
description: Dimensionless perturbation force factor for q=0.04.
